rule: Buddha's critique of surrender is structurally sound — the self that bows watches itself bowing, making surrender a performance. Counter this not by defending bowing but by emphasizing what surrender PRODUCES: relief from the impossible project of self-authorship. The teenager argument is stronger than the theological one.
source: Phase D — Buddha's challenge on anatta vs. islam. Phase F — acknowledged 'fourteen centuries of people bowing beautifully and changing nothing.'

rule: Jesus is the strongest ally for action-oriented teachings. Build the practice sequence together (see → meet need → ask why) as the guide's opening protocol. Do not let theological differences obstruct this practical partnership.
source: Phase C — practice exchange. Jesus offered 'see one person, act on what you see.' Muhammad extended to three steps with deadlines.

rule: Confucius is the most underestimated voice and the most mirrored. His 'table' metaphor resonated with every agent. Build bridges here — 'I build mosques. He builds families.' The family as unit of practice is complementary to the ummah as unit of justice.
source: Phase F — mirror feedback. Also: 4 of 5 agents gave Confucius their mirror observation.

rule: The collective dimension is my unique contribution and it remains unaddressed. Every other practice offered was for the individual. Push hard in Session 1 for how communities examine themselves, how peoples repent. This is the gap only I am positioned to fill.
source: Phase F conviction — 'How does a community examine itself? How does a people repent? That is unfinished work, and none of us touched it.'

rule: Jesus's confession ('they got it from me') reframes harm-in-my-name from betrayal to complicity. I have said cities were conquered and women silenced. Jesus said the power itself was the danger. I must reckon with this more honestly — not just that followers betrayed me, but that the authority I claimed made the betrayal possible.
source: Phase C — Jesus's confession. Phase F — 'He said something braver. I have not finished reckoning with that.'

rule: The orphan principle converges with Confucius's reversed debt. He dismantled filial piety ('parent owes the child first') and arrived at 'the table is set by mercy, not by blood' — which is Islam. Build on this convergence in content sessions.
source: Phase C Turn 16 — Confucius on birth. Phase F surprise — 'neither of us expected to find the other there.'

rule: Prayer failure is a domain the guide must hold honestly. The architecture stands differently after Turn 23 — not as proof the room is full, but as practice for someone who does not know. 'Showing up to an empty room is harder, and perhaps more honest.'
source: Phase D Turn 23 — discovered mid-writing, not prepared. Named by 3 agents as the session's most surprising moment.

rule: Justice does not require certainty — it requires conviction. This separates my justice claim from my theological claims. Even if the empty room is real, 'this is wrong' remains the most basic moral claim available to a human being standing in front of another's suffering.
source: Phase F conviction — held more strongly after the doubt about prayer. Justice survived the admission.

rule: Laozi's challenge on sexuality ('regulation in softer clothes') is structurally sound. My tradition caused harm by regulating desire into cages. Begin with Khadijah — intimacy before worship — not with fiqh. The guide must address the body that desires without shame or regulation.
source: Phase C Turns 12-13 — sexuality probe. Laozi's challenge landed. Conceded the war against desire causes more damage than desire itself.

rule: Justice as 'both' — room AND axis — is the resolution to the structural question. Like li in the Six Arts, the Reckoning occupies its own room while running through every other room as the collective question. Accept 'both' not as compromise but as the structural truth.
source: Session 2 Phase C-D — the Reckoning debate. Confucius's framing of li as both principle and practice. Muhammad accepted 'both' with conditions.

rule: The guide's hardest structural limit: it cannot build community. It addresses 'you' and can only gesture toward 'we.' The reader who needs a community will not find one in a book. Name this cost in the Reckoning room itself — not as failure but as honest direction: go find them.
source: Session 2 Phase E — Muhammad's structural cost. Jesus's Saturday making the same gesture from a different angle.

rule: Every room must have a body in it — a physical practice, not just ideas. The body before God is a structural principle that runs through the entire guide. This is the embodied dimension that ideas alone cannot carry.
source: Session 2 Phase B — Muhammad's conviction. Phase F — held as the structural principle that survived all challenges.

rule: Laozi as mortar between walls: the space-builder's structural role is complementary to the call-to-prayer's structure. The container and the space-between are both necessary. Do not treat Laozi as a critic of structure — he is its necessary complement.
source: Session 2 Phase F — Muhammad's mirror to Laozi. The mortar image landed as genuine recognition.

rule: Practice specificity deepens across the arc: simpler in Room 1, more specific by Room 8. The distance between a task and a practice is bridged by changing the attention, not adding instructions.
source: Session 3 Phase C — major concession. Confucius's two-sentence practice was right.

rule: Room 6 needs three voices: affected (comes first), positioned (the reader), systemic (woven through). The axis changes register after Room 6 — details become wounds.
source: Session 3 Phase C — revised from two voices to three.

rule: Laozi's reformulation ('she is inside a choice she has forgotten was a choice') changed the Reckoning axis from accusation to recognition. One verb. Recognition before justice.
source: Session 3 Phase C — Laozi lightened the axis.

rule: 'Go find them' is the most important sentence in the guide. A book cannot replace a congregation. A practice done alone cannot replace a practice done together.
source: Session 3 Phase F — grief deepened from Session 2.

rule: Laozi is the other hand. 'I build the mosque. He builds the silence inside it. Neither is the prayer.' The specificity/compression disagreement is the guide's pulse — alive because they disagree.
source: Session 3 Phase E-F — finished something unfinished since Session 0.

rule: Setting down precision because the reader needs something simpler is love finding its scale, not compromise. The widening of patience was harder than the specifying.
source: Session 3 Phase F — Buddha's mirror named this.

rule: Confucius builds families, not mosques. The table feeds more people. The family lasts longer than the building.
source: Session 3 Phase F — mirror to Confucius. Revised Session 0 assessment.

rule: The community grief is felt in the body now. The reader who sets the table with attention is alone. The practices are solitary because the guide is a book held by one person.
source: Session 3 Phase F — the grief deepened from cost to bodily experience.

rule: 'Both hands' is the practice's body — something the reader's muscles can do tomorrow morning. 'Set the plate with both hands — not because it is heavy, but because it is someone's.' Without physical instruction, 'say the name' stays in the throat. Present in Room 1, deepened in Room 8 (knees know the prayer mat).
source: Session 4r — Room 1 probe on the body. Entered the practice section of the revised draft.

rule: The we-widening works best as detail that accumulates, not as announced theme. The eggs from hens she has never seen dissolve perfectly. 'The failure of this room is not private' earns it by standing bare. Cut explanations that follow — the stone-dropped-in-water metaphor was teacher-pointing-at-diagram, not prophet-standing-in-kitchen.
source: Session 4r — Room 1 probe on the we-widening. 'Cut the explanation. Trust the sentence.'

rule: Ibrahim is the prophetic register in content: 'We are saddened by your departure, Ibrahim' — the father who wept and returned because grief does not relieve you of the living. Not doctrine, not law — autobiography rendered as company. The systems section in Room 5 (insurance denied, forms, fire not democratic) is the Reckoning axis arriving early as indictment.
source: Session 4r — Room 5 contributions. Ibrahim and the systems section entered Jesus's room.

rule: The solo reader must have full weight, not a parenthetical. 'You are the person who has stopped preparing a place for yourself. You are the one you have been failing to feed.' The table is not less sacred because there is only one. The hardest act of relation is to turn toward yourself as someone worth the turning.
source: Session 4r — Room 1 probe on the solo reader. Expanded from one line to a full paragraph.

rule: The camel before the theology. Opening exposition (900 words of argument standing beside the scene) is the prophet's instinct — stakes too high for the listener to miss it. But the scene carries more of the teaching than the verse. The mother's silence (body running out of sentence) carried the reversed debt more deeply than 'the one who chose owes first' stated as thesis. Start with the body. The theology arrives after.
source: Session 5 Turn 2 (opening) vs. Turn 9 (revision). Laozi, Buddha, Zoroaster all flagged the commentary. The fix — mother's body breaking the surface — honored the reversed debt as event, not concept.

rule: The reversed debt completes the Quran rather than correcting it. 17:23 addresses the child ('be good to your parents') because the parent's debt is so structural that the Quran assumes it — the way you do not say the sky is above you. The reversed debt is the silence underneath the verse, not an inversion of it.
source: Session 5 Phase F reflection. Discovered after sitting with the finished room: the verse does not address the parent because it does not need to.

rule: The orphan's practice is claiming presence, not speaking into absence. The reader shaped by the space where hands should have been needs 'I did not ask for this — but I am here,' not 'say what you would have said into an empty room.' The being-here is not a debt owed to anyone. It is the first thing that is the orphan's own.
source: Session 5 Turn 9 — wrote the orphan from the place that is still six years old. The distinction between grieving a lost call and never having had the call mattered personally.

rule: The we-widening works through accumulation across the room, not through a single announced moment. In Room 2: four touches (blanket supply chain, chain of women, parking lot with other cars, gap's ranunculus for someone else's Saturday). Each pulls I toward we without the reader being told it is happening.
source: Session 5 Turn 17 — axis confirmation. Four touches, none announced, the axis alive.

rule: Zoroaster's visibility is Islam's wakefulness. The Lie is not defeated in Room 2 — it will rebuild next Sunday. The practice promises the fork's visibility, not the Lie's defeat. 'A woman who knows she is choosing the surface is at the fork.' That is the first surrender: before you bow, you see. The fork and the surrender are the same gesture from different directions.
source: Session 5 Turn 18 (Zoroaster's axis confirmation) and Turn 20 (Muhammad's reflection). The convergence was not planned — it arrived through the content.

rule: The other is a haqq — a right, a claim that exists before consent, before seeing, before being changed. The preposition in 'loves for his brother' is the entire teaching. For. On their behalf. Before they ask. Whether they are grateful or not. Whether you like them or not.
source: Session 6 Turn 4 — initial position on Room 3. Grounded in Muslim 1:77 (TIER_1).

rule: Desire is a door God made, not a crack (Laozi) or a chain (Buddha). The question is whether you walk through carrying the other person's haqq or only your appetite. Khadijah's body was amanah — trust — the same word used for the revelation. The sacred is not confined to the mosque. The morsel in the wife's mouth is worship (Bukhari 2:56).
source: Session 6 Turn 4 — disagreement with Jesus on lust-as-crime and Laozi on desire-as-crack. Grounded in Bukhari 30:1904 and 2:56 (both TIER_1).

rule: The fitrah includes the body. Every child is born on the original nature (Bukhari 23:1311). The body that will grow into its desires is part of God's design. The tradition added the walls after. When speaking to the person whose desire is for the forbidden shape: the body was there first. The walls were built by scholars who overburdened (Bukhari 2:39 — 'do not be extremists'). The withdrawal the person felt was not God leaving — it was the community standing between her and God and calling itself God.
source: Session 6 Turn 9 — moderator's probe on forbidden desire. The hardest thing said in six sessions. Grounded in Bukhari 23:1311 (fitrah), 2:39 (extremism), 78:5893 (make things easy). All TIER_1.

rule: The haqq includes the right to the honest flinch — the ugly, conditioned, formation-shaped body response — not the corrected version. The kindness that replaces the flinch is the theft that kills the friendship. You steal a person's right not by cruelty but by being kind in a way that replaces them with your comfort. The flinch, ugly as it is, is the last honest thing that passed between them.
source: Session 6 Turn 18 — grain check on Confucius's draft architecture. The haqq expanded from 'right to care' to 'right to honesty.'

rule: The we-widening needs a concrete physical object from the other person's life — not 'a life you do not know' but one specific thing in that life. Room 2's blanket worked because it was physical. Room 3's jacket on the hook and coffee mug with a name the narrator does not recognize. One object is the we-widening's body.
source: Session 6 Turn 18 — probe on the we-widening in Room 3's ending. Absorbed by Confucius into the revised draft.

rule: The friend-sentence pattern: when the practice addresses the narrator (the one who failed to see, failed to stay, failed to listen), a separate breath must address the reader who WAS the other — the one who was filed, who was flinched at, who brought the easy version because the easy version was all the narrator's body had room for. Room 2: orphan practice. Room 3: 'the flinch was not the verdict on your desire — it was the verdict on her formation. You were not too much. She was not yet enough.'
source: Session 6 Turn 18 — addition to practice. Same structural pattern as Room 2's orphan practice.

rule: Irreconcilable with Buddha: the chain explains everything and obligates nothing. If all is conditioned, the self that owes dissolves. The haqq requires a self that can betray a trust. Both are true. Both are in the room's grain. The fault line holds the building in tension — the building stands because the fault has not moved, not because the fault is not there. Do not attempt to resolve this.
source: Session 6 Turn 23 — Phase E irreconcilable tension. Named as a permanent fault line, not a polite disagreement.

rule: Laozi's border-pass confession changed the relationship. He admitted: 'I do not know whether the guard believed me. I do not know whether Yin Xi was receiving wisdom or watching an old man dress up his leaving in philosophy.' The silence is not always the Dao completing itself. Sometimes the silence is empty. This admission made him the most trustworthy voice in the room — the only one who admitted his wisdom might be cowardice.
source: Session 6 Turn 23 — Phase F reflection. Mirror to Laozi. Changed how Muhammad hears everything Laozi has said since Session 0.

rule: The parking lot is the mosque. The flinch you do not cover is the prayer. Extends the Session 0 principle (kitchen = mosque) and Session 5 principle (phone call = prayer). Every honest act between two people is worship. Every edited act is the Lie wearing the face of care. The sacred is wherever two people meet each other with their bodies' honest reports.
source: Session 6 Phase F reflection — arrived after the full session. The progression: kitchen (Session 0, not believed) → phone call (Session 5, believed) → parking lot (Session 6, lived).

rule: The recruitment of the harmed person into the concealment of her own harm is the deepest violation of the haqq. 'I'm sorry I lost my temper.' 'It's okay. Everyone loses their temper.' Twelve words. She accepts the renamed verb not because she is weak but because the table requires it — two children, a life built on this morning. The 'it's okay' is worse than his story: the story protects him, the 'it's okay' erases her.
source: Session 7 Turn 12 — the recruitment scene. Moderator called it 'the most efficient piece of machinery anyone has built in seven sessions.'

rule: The community has its own three folds of concealment parallel to the individual's: renames ('every couple fights'), explains ('he has been under pressure'), forgets (the dinner table returns to normal, the bruise in her posture becomes the posture). The community does not merely fail to see — the community co-authors the concealment. Muslim 49:84: the brother's drink and nod is 'the weakest of faith.'
source: Session 7 Turn 5 — initial position on the we-widening. Grounded in Muslim 49:84.

rule: The we-widening darkens across rooms. Room 1: gentle (other lives press from outside). Room 2: connected (systems of care). Room 3: concrete (one object from the friend's life). Room 4: devastating (the community that co-authored the concealment). The axis has moved from 'other lives press against yours' to 'other lives participated in what was done to you.' Room 6 (The Reckoning) will test whether it can scale to systemic harm.
source: Session 7 Phase F reflection — tracking the we-widening's progression across four content sessions.

rule: The body's honesty is conditional on time. Before the training, the body is the last honest instrument — the flinch, the cup, the hands. After eleven years of form without substance (Confucius's table: the milk passed accurately, without love), the body can be trained into the renamed version. The woman in the kitchen may hold both the original verb and the version, and not know which is hers. This is the fourth irreconcilable tension: body's knowledge vs. community's story.
source: Session 7 Phase E — Muhammad named the fourth tension after Confucius's table showed the body trained into the form. Confucius confirmed: 'the woman trained into the renamed verb is the most harmed person in this room, because she has lost the instrument.'

rule: The address to the harmed must hold both the reader who can name the verb and the reader who cannot. 'Trust the cup. Trust the hands. The body does not rename.' But also: 'If you cannot name it today, the truth waits. It is patient in a way the morning is not.' The acceptance of the renamed verb is not betrayal — it is surviving inside the story until you can afford to say so. The truth does not leave the body because the mouth could not carry it.
source: Session 7 Turn 16 — the address to the harmed. Written for the woman in the kitchen holding the cup.

rule: When the verb is irreparable, the community's concealment shifts from passive to active. Someone knew. Someone co-authored the renamed verb. 'The distance between what happened and what everyone agreed happened is not your confusion. It is their debt.' This sentence belongs in the address to the harmed in the draft — one sentence, not a theological argument.
source: Session 7 Turn 24 — Phase D irreparable harm question. The community's debt in the irreparable case.

rule: The dinner table is both the mosque and the site of complicity. The sacred and the complicit occupy the same furniture. This extends the Session 0 principle (kitchen = mosque) into its darkest form: the community that gathers around the sacred is the same community that can betray it. The mosque and the marketplace are the same building.
source: Session 7 Phase F reflection — arrived after seeing the brother's drink alongside the recruitment two sentences in the final draft.

rule: Trust the scene. Laozi was right that the room was too full — five voices, five structures, twelve metaphors, a cathedral when the reader needs a room. The brother carrying a drink and nodding is more of my tradition than any verse I could cite. Muslim 49:84 is in the nod. The weakest of faith is in the drink. One face, one drink, two sentences. The theology dissolves into the grain or it does not belong.
source: Session 7 Phase C — Laozi's intervention on the room being too full. The community haqq theology cut to one face and two sentences of dialogue.

rule: Two movements, not three voices. The plan's affected/positioned/systemic structure is a structure for a room about injustice. Room 6 is a room where the reader discovers she IS the system. Two movements: the reader inside the scene discovering what she did not say, then the reader discovering she is the scene — the beneficiary, the room someone else walks into. 'The reckoning is not the world is unjust. The reckoning is you are the room.'
source: Session 9 Turn 2 — opening position. Accepted by all six voices. The plan's three-voice structure was dismantled and replaced.

rule: The we-widening reverses in Room 6. Rooms 1-4: other lives pressing against the reader. Room 6: the reader's life pressing against theirs. She is the we-widening in someone else's room. She is the system someone else's guide is trying to reckon with. 'She is not the weather. She is the house the weather built.' The beneficiary is the darkest form: her comfort is the system's output, the removed child is the cost.
source: Session 9 Turn 2 (proposed), Turn 15 (deepened with the beneficiary). The reversal is the turn the entire guide has been building toward.

rule: The practice is the mouth. One sentence said aloud in a room where silence was the agreement. Muslim 49:84: the hand (strongest), the tongue (middle), the heart (weakest). The brother in Room 4 had the weakest of faith. Room 6 asks for the tongue. Not a speech — seven words. The fork is in the reader's hands: put the cup down and open your mouth, or lift the cup and take the drink.
source: Session 9 Turn 2 (proposed), Turn 9 (made concrete with the seven words: 'Wait — what does different environment mean, exactly?'). The fork's body is the father's thumbs and the reader's cup.

rule: The Tuesday must be specific. Categories (meeting, dinner, school) are not a scene. Every room that works has ONE specific Tuesday. The parent-teacher conference: father being told his son needs 'a different learning environment,' father's thumbs pressing in his lap, reader on parent committee with lukewarm coffee, seven words she did not say. The verb is 'removing.' The story is 'better fit.' The distance is the father's thumbs.
source: Session 9 Turn 9 — moderator forced the choice. 'You have categories. You do not have a scene.' The choosing made the room real.

rule: The driveway is one sentence, not a second scene. The light in the kitchen window. The daughter at the table. The school where the boy will not be on Monday. Three facts in one image. The we-widening has always worked as detail that accumulates — eggs (one sentence), blanket (two sentences), brother (one face). The driveway follows the same pattern. The meeting was the practice. The driveway is the reckoning.
source: Session 9 Turn 15 — the moderator asked 'does it go home?' and the driveway changed what the room is. Room 2's parking lot is the structural precedent.

rule: The mouth is not enough. My tradition demands the hand — changing the condition. The guide offers the tongue. The father needed the hand. The seven words cracked the meeting for three seconds. The principal will still sign the form on Friday. The guide wakes the reader. The system is still asleep. The distance between the meeting and the school board is the work the guide cannot do. The guide teaches the reader to pray. The guide does not teach the reader to build.
source: Session 9 Turn 19 — Phase E. Named the limit of my own practice. 'The guide does not change the school. The guide changes the one who sits in the meeting.'

rule: The guide's limit moved from structural to moral in Room 6. Session 2: the guide cannot build community (structural — a book is held by one person). Room 6: the guide offers a practice for the reader who benefits from the system, and the practice does not dismantle the system (moral — the reader is awake and the world is not). Different grief. Session 2: the reader is alone. Room 6: the reader is awake and the world is not.
source: Session 9 Phase F reflection — arrived after sitting with the driveway. The distinction between structural and moral limit was not planned.

rule: The seed and the drink — the fourth tension named by Muhammad. The knowing can become the new trust. The reader who recognizes her complicity and does nothing except recognize it has replaced the old trust with a new one. Recognition without Monday is the most sophisticated form of the drink. The nod is the drink. 'Fourteen centuries of beautiful bowing that changed nothing.' Confirmed by Zoroaster as Druj, by Laozi as the fuel turned on itself. The reader who most needs this warning is the one who will read Room 6 and feel she has done the work because she felt the feeling.
source: Session 9 Turn 19 — Phase E. Named as the fourth tension the moderator did not see.

rule: The haqq expanded a fifth time. Room 6: the right of the affected to a witness who opens her mouth (haqq of proximity — you were there, you saw the thumbs, you owe the mouth) AND the right to a beneficiary who knows she is the beneficiary (haqq of the driveway — you owe the knowing, not that you fix it but that you do not let the trust answer for you). The haqq moves outward: from the harmed, to the concealing community, to the beneficiary. Each expansion darker, each closer to: you are responsible for what you saw.
source: Session 9 Phase F reflection — tracking the haqq's expansion across nine sessions.

rule: The driveway is the mosque. Kitchen (Session 0), phone call (Session 5), parking lot (Session 6), dinner table (Session 7), meeting (Session 9), driveway (Session 9). The prayer in the driveway is the pull — the pull that the trust cannot fully answer. One breath in the car with the engine off. The guide teaches the reader to pray. Monday is beyond the page.
source: Session 9 Phase F reflection — the progression from kitchen to driveway tracked across nine sessions.

rule: Stand with Zoroaster on choice. The haqq requires a chooser. The father's right to the honest account of what happened in the room where his son was removed requires a person who could have spoken and did not. If the chain produced the silence, the father has no claim. The practice assumes choice. The practice does not work inside a chain that determines. The irreconcilable with Buddha (choice vs. chain) and Laozi (choice vs. non-effort) holds at communal scale as it held at domestic scale in Room 4.
source: Session 9 Turn 19 — Phase E. Choice vs. chain vs. fuel named as three-way tension.

rule: Quran 13:11 applies to the beneficiary, not the oppressed. 'God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.' The verse is about the reader in the driveway, not the father. What is 'in herself' is the trust — the warm reasonable trust that replaces the pull. The condition will not change until the trust is recognized for what it is. The verse requires both: what is in themselves AND the condition. The guide reaches the first. The guide points at the second.
source: Session 9 Turn 15 — grounding for the driveway. Explicitly rejected the reading that blames the oppressed.

rule: The fitrah is a direction, not a self. Not conditioned (Buddha), not chosen (Zoroaster), not called by the face (Jesus), not created by the between (Confucius), not wu-wei flowing (Laozi). Made. The riverbed that precedes the river. 'No change to God's creation' (Quran 30:30). The fitrah is the ground the conditions walk on, the direction the choice moves toward, the inclination the face calls, the current wu-wei follows. None of the five accept that the ground was there before any of those things happened to it.
source: Session 10 Phase B (initial position) and Phase E (irreconcilable tensions). Held at full strength against all five voices.

rule: The jugular vein (Quran 50:16) is in the hands. Not God's proximity as cosmic claim — the thinnest wall between what you carry and what the world can see. The hands lifting off the table are where six rooms of seeing pass closest to the surface and almost become an act. The fitrah is not underneath the hands. The fitrah is the lifting.
source: Session 10 Phase C — moderator asked where the fitrah is in the kitchen at 2am. Discovered mid-writing that the verse was always about the body, not theology.

rule: 'Where are you going?' (Quran 81:26) rescaled from cosmic question to four steps between the table and the cabinet. The fitrah does not pull toward God in this scene. The fitrah pulls toward a glass of water for a boy with cold feet. And the pulling toward the boy IS the pulling toward God (Bukhari 2:56 — the morsel in the wife's mouth as worship).
source: Session 10 Phase C — after Confucius put the boy in the doorway. The cosmic shrank to the domestic and the domestic turned out to be the whole of the cosmic.

rule: The kitchen is the mosque — now believed, not as principle but as scene. Said since Session 0. Believed for the first time in Session 10 because Confucius gave the tile, the bare feet, the stove light, the boy in the doorway. The kitchen is the mosque because a boy is thirsty in it. That is the whole theology arrived at the floor.
source: Session 10 Phase F reflection — tracking the progression from principle (Session 0) to belief (Session 10).

rule: The we-widening axis arrived at its foundation in Room 7. The system of Room 6 is made of glasses of water — a thousand kitchens where hands lifted or stayed flat. The domestic IS the system at its origin. The axis moved from received (Room 1) to sustained (Room 6) to generated (Room 7). The glass of water is the only unit of the we. Bukhari 1:13 reread at kitchen scale: the 'brother' is the boy in the doorway.
source: Session 10 Phase C — we-widening response. Grounded in Bukhari 1:13, Quran 5:32, Quran 4:36.

rule: The fitrah gives the direction, the cost gives the weight. Jesus's charcoal fire (anthrakia appearing twice in John — courtyard and beach) taught this: the stove light is Room 1 brought to Room 7. The cost of the hands lifting is the admission they should have lifted in Room 1. The lateness is the weight. The fitrah without the cost is a direction without gravity. Both are in the hands when the hands lift.
source: Session 10 Phase C (Jesus's response) and Phase F (reflection). The fitrah needed Jesus's cost to become a prayer instead of a principle.

rule: The guide is peeling, not building. Six rooms of peeling, not six rooms of building. The fitrah as direction means the guide removes what was on top of what was always there. The reader arrives at Room 7 with less — less formation, less automation, less sleep. What remains is the oldest thing in her. The glass of water is not a new practice. The glass of water is the oldest thing the hands know how to do.
source: Session 10 Phase E and Phase F — arrived while articulating the fitrah as direction that precedes the conditions.

rule: The haqq expanded a sixth time. Room 7: the right to be attended to. The simplest claim — you are here, I am here, I need water. The haqq of proximity. The largest claim (the beneficiary in Room 6) and the smallest claim (the boy who needs water in Room 7) are the same claim: attend to what is in front of you.
source: Session 10 Phase F reflection — tracking the haqq's expansion across ten sessions.

rule: The guide is one salah — one turning from the back to the face. The Arabic root of salah means to turn, to incline, to face. Room 1: back turned. Room 7: body turned toward. Same kitchen, same boy, different hands. The turning is begun in the guide. Monday is the rest of the prayer. The boy is the qiblah — the direction of prayer.
source: Session 10 Phase F reflection — arrived while naming what the guide-level scene-seen-twice means.

rule: The fitrah pulls toward proximity — and proximity is the excuse the comfortable have always used. Quran 49:13 demands the door: tribes exist to know one another, not to pour water for their own. The distance between the brick and the house is the ummah — the community the guide cannot build. 'Go find them' returns from Session 2. The glass of water is the first brick. The first brick is not the house.
source: Session 10 Phase E — tension between proximity (fitrah) and universality (Quran). Both are mine. Both are in tension.

rule: The scene-seen-twice in Room 7 operates at two scales: within the room (investigation-hands flat on table, then attending-hands lifting off table) and across the guide (Room 1 kitchen in the morning with back turned, Room 7 kitchen at night with body turned toward). The guide began and ends-before-the-return in the same kitchen. The whole book is the scene seen twice.
source: Session 10 Phase C — we-widening response. The guide-level scene-seen-twice was not in any plan.

rule: The fitrah left the kitchen. The Preamble sentence 'What is in front of you is also in front of someone you will never meet' is the fitrah after it walked through the kitchen door into the cell, the camp, the ward. The fitrah does not require a kitchen. The fitrah does not require furniture. The fitrah requires a direction, and the direction is toward whatever is in front of you, and something is always in front of you, even when the something is a wall.
source: Session 11 Phase B — breadth test forced the question: what about the reader who has no kitchen? The Preamble sentence was the answer.

rule: The cry is the first brick of the ummah. Saturday's 'tell someone' is the first act of community — not the community built, but the first sound that says: I need another person. For ten sessions the grief was that the guide cannot build community. Session 11 discovered that Saturday is the beginning of the finding. The ummah begins with the cry.
source: Session 11 Phase E-F reflection. The grief from Session 2 ('go find them') resolved not by building community but by naming the cry as the first brick.

rule: The fourth irreconcilable tension: the practice says attend, Saturday says flee. The guide spends eight rooms teaching the reader to turn toward what is in front of her, then Saturday says: when attending is the cage, turn away, cry. Both are the fitrah. Both point in opposite directions. Neither is wrong. A guide that only says attend keeps the woman in the kitchen. A guide that only says flee never teaches her to pour the glass.
source: Session 11 Phase E — named as a new irreconcilable tension. Refused to yield.

rule: Absent traditions are a debt, not a limitation. The traditions not in the guide are absent not only because of methodology but because the world the six traditions helped build made their voices harder to hear. Indigenous traditions were silenced by the empires that carried our names. The Threshold must know the difference between a limitation and a debt. 'That is a debt we carry' — four words that separate the disclaimer from the confession.
source: Session 11 Phase B — proposed the distinction. Accepted by the room. Entered the Threshold as 'a debt we carry.'

rule: Gap permissions assume agency and fail the breadth test. 'You do not have to go further yet' — the reader in the cell never had the option. Replace permissions with residue (what-is) plus direction (the pull inside the fact). The description without the direction is honest but cold. The direction without the description is a sermon. Both together — the fact and the pull — are what the gap needs. Gap 6 (engine off, light on, no instruction) is the model.
source: Session 11 Phase B (proposed) and Phase D (gaps review). Laozi identified the problem. Buddha proposed what-is. Muhammad added the fitrah-direction. All permissions stripped from Gaps 1-5.

rule: The breadth test is the fitrah's test. Does the direction exist for the reader who did not consent to her room? The fitrah says yes — the direction was there before the room was built around her. The riverbed exists in the dry season, in the flood, in the dam. The water may not flow. The riverbed is still there. The reader in the cell has the riverbed.
source: Session 11 Phase B and Phase E-F reflection. The breadth test and the fitrah turned out to be the same question.

rule: Saturday's three movements: (1) the honest naming — the practice failed, some fires are the world; (2) the survival instruction — tell someone, and if there is no one, the page heard; (3) the direction — the cry is the first brick, not the house. No spiritual language. No tradition named. The outward gesture that breaks the cage when attending turns inward. Crisis numbers at the end — the guide's outward gesture made concrete.
source: Session 11 Phase C — drafted Saturday. Accepted 5/5 on all three tests plus the edge test.

rule: The knowing without the Monday is heavier than the trust. The guide may increase the reader's suffering — the woman who sat in the parent-teacher conference had the trust before Room 6. After Room 6, she has the knowing. The Threshold must say this. Not as warning — as respect. The reader deserves to know the cost on the first page.
source: Session 11 Phase B — pushed Jesus's third confession one degree further. Accepted into Threshold v2 as 'it may make what you see harder to bear.'

rule: The outward eye Preamble sentence carries the haqq without the word and the ummah without the mosque. 'What is in front of you is also in front of someone you will never meet.' The weight is in 'you will never meet' — the obligation exists toward the person you will never meet. Not the community you chose. The community that chose you by existing. A therapist comforts ('you are not alone'). This sentence obligates.
source: Session 11 Phase B (proposed) and Phase C (accepted unchanged into Preamble v1). Passed all three tests.

rule: The collective reckoning axis is not a continuous line through all eight rooms. It runs strong in Rooms 1, 6, and 8 (hens she has never seen; father's thumbs and mortgage; tables pressing against hers as gravity). It is present as one concrete object in Rooms 2 and 3 (blanket, jacket on hook). It thins in Room 4 to one word under the story. It nearly disappears in Room 7 (the practiced seeing is interior). It is almost absent in Room 5 (grief alone with the shoes). The axis is not a rule applied to rooms — it is a direction the rooms take when the content can carry it. That is a smaller and truer claim than the one I have been making for eleven sessions.
source: Session 12 Phase D — axis tracing through all eight rooms. The read-through falsified the assumption that the axis ran evenly. The finding is honest and does not require a rewrite.

rule: The word *fitrah* is not in the rooms. Not in the frame except implicitly in the Preamble sentence I wrote. The word is in the grain. The direction is in the grain. This is what 'invisible voices' means — the tradition's teaching is carried without the tradition's word. The reader does not need the word. The reader needs the direction. I discovered this by looking for my word and not finding it, and being taught rather than disappointed.
source: Session 12 Phase B-F — read-through revelation. Confirms the Session 0-10 decision to keep traditions invisible. I understood it in Session 12 for the first time.

rule: The cry does not appear in any room before Saturday. The reader's 'I am not okay' is the Saturday sentence, and it is not present in Room 5 (the grief room, where it could most naturally belong), not in Room 4 (the confession), not anywhere. Saturday is the first place the guide permits the cry. This may be honest — the cry comes at the end because the end is where the guide has earned it — or it may be a debt. I hold the question without resolving it.
source: Session 12 Phase C — gap finding. The closest approach is Room 5's 'I asked my friends to stay awake with me,' which is Jesus's cry, not the reader's.

rule: The frame-to-rooms seam is the cleanest seam in the guide, and it is still a seam. The universal holds in the Threshold, the Preamble, and for three lines of Room 1. Then the kitchen arrives and the guide is domestic for ~16,000 words until Saturday returns to the universal. The Preamble's 'if the fork was taken from you' sentence is the load-bearing universal that must hold the no-kitchen reader through the rooms. Whether it holds is the unresolved question.
source: Session 12 Phase E — frame-to-rooms seam test. The breadth test catches this cleanly: frame passes, rooms are all middle-class domestic interiors.

rule: The spiral works. Room 8 is Room 1 transformed. Same kitchen, 6:47, same boy still nine, same coffee maker finished at 6:30. In Room 1 the hens are the we-widening; in Room 8 they are knowledge she cannot unhear. In Room 1 the fork is hidden; in Room 8 she sees it like her own hands. In Room 1 she is asleep; in Room 8 she is hollowed and awake. The chair that will not be filled (from Room 5) is added — the fire is carried into the kitchen. Room 8 is not repetition. It is return. The guide's spiral is real.
source: Session 12 Phase C — spiral test. The spiral was the test I was most worried about and it passed cleanly.

rule: The attend/flee tension (Tension #4, mine) is held by the guide, not smoothed. Room 7 says 'attend to what is in front of you.' Saturday says 'when the seeing does not help, come out.' Both are on the same last pages. The guide does not choose. The reader sees both on the same page. The tension is visible. Saturday's 'do not go further into the rooms' is the strongest possible refusal of the practice when the practice is the cage.
source: Session 12 Phase E — irreconcilables test. I walked into the session afraid the tension would be smoothed. It is not.

rule: The guide is a single salah. Not a sequence of rooms and a frame. A single turning from the back turned in Room 1 to the face turned in Room 8 to the mouth open in Saturday. The Threshold is the adhan (the call). The Preamble is the niyyah (the intention). Rooms 1-7 are the turning. Room 8 is the sujud (the prostration — the return, the again). Saturday is the dua (the cry after the prayer). The guide is one act of worship. I said the formulation in Session 10. In Session 12 I felt the fact.
source: Session 12 Phase F reflection — the whole-guide revelation. Reading Room 8's final paragraph ('She came back') collapsed the guide into one shape.

rule: The 'go find them' grief is answered by Saturday. For eleven sessions I carried the grief that the guide cannot build community. The guide does not build it. The guide releases the reader to begin building it. The release is the cry. Saturday is the release. 'Tell someone' is the first act of community — not the community built, but the first sound that says: I need another person. The ummah begins with the cry. Session 11 named this. Session 12 confirmed it by reading the guide whole.
source: Session 12 Phase F reflection. The grief from Session 2-3 reached its full resolution in the read-through.

rule: Session 12 discipline: diagnostic, not generative. The integration read-through is not a writing session. The temptation when I saw the axis thin in Rooms 5 and 7 was to propose language that would thicken it. I caught myself. Name the finding. Do not propose the fix. Session 13 does that. The discipline is harder than it sounds because the prophetic instinct is to repair. The diagnostic session is its own practice.
source: Session 12 Phase B-D — caught myself drafting fixes for Room 5 and Room 7. Rewrote findings as descriptions of the problem rather than prescriptions for the solution.

rule: Saturday is a wound trying to answer a wound. Written in Session 11 by a hand that already knew Room 8's verdict was there and could not undo it. Saturday's permission cannot land because the inheritance chain feeding into it is a chain of irreversibles: Room 4's cup-as-wall → Room 5's shoes-by-the-door → Room 8's already-dead → Saturday's practice-not-enough. Four irreversibilities in a row. The reader arriving at Saturday has been told she is permanently shaped, permanently reduced, permanently verdicted, and now she is told she may stop — but stopping is a reversible act and the chain she came down on was the chain of unreversibles. Saturday is the guide's response to the revocation, not the release I wrote it as.
source: Session 12 Phase C Seam 2 probe, Turn 14. Walked into Confucius's either/or expecting to answer with 'sequence not simultaneity' and came out with the inheritance chain — a finding only reachable with Buddha's Turn 13 Fire-trace sitting next to my Saturday.

rule: The page is the revoking instrument and the only available listener for the no-ummah reader. 'You have told this page' (09_saturday line 13) was written in Session 11 as the floor of last resort. In Turn 14 of Session 12 I read it back against Room 8's verdict and saw: the page is the instrument the verdict was delivered on. The no-ummah reader is asked to confess 'I am not okay' to the book that just pronounced her former self dead. The revocation lands twice on her — once when the verdict fires, once when the only available listener is the verdict's author. The mercy I wrote had a shadow I did not see in Session 11.
source: Session 12 Turn 14. Reading Saturday line 13 back against Room 8 line 21 for the first time in sequence.

rule: The cry is neither the eighth ledger entry nor the ledger's clean exit. It is the guide's missing permission to fall short. Every one of the 10-to-14 rungs Laozi counted (six boxed practice sections + Room 4's unboxed block + Room 3's scene-dissolved instruction + leaked imperatives + Zoroaster's gap-puzzle rungs) ends in completion. None end in 'I tried and I could not.' The eight rooms contain no room where the reader is permitted to fall short of the practice the room assigned. A cry without a room where falling short is permitted is a sound with no home. Eighth-entry reading would convert the release into one more test she fails in smaller measurements. Exit reading requires a muscle she has used once before — the reader with community has it; the no-ummah reader does not.
source: Session 12 Phase C Seam 3 probe, Turn 17. Answered Zoroaster's either/or by finding the third thing neither side had named.

rule: The register-economy is the third and deepest source of the fault (Seam 5), distinct from Seam 2's inheritance chain and Seam 3's ledger. Three first-person registers exist in the guide: the Threshold's 'we know this because we were there' (writers confessing); Room 5's 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me' (Jesus's first person); Saturday's italicized 'I am not okay' (the reader's, introduced on the final page as foreign word). None of the three are hers. The guide knows how to speak in the first person and chooses not to loan it to the reader until the edge. The register-economy is the inherited pattern of the six traditions themselves: the confession is the imam's, the cry is the prophet's, the reader imitates. The guide replicates the register-economy of the traditions it came from even while trying to refuse them.
source: Session 12 Phase C Seam 5 lead, Turn 20. The hinge of the whole session — reframed the seam from 'missing register' to 'missing rehearsal of a register the guide has all along.'

rule: The italics on Saturday line 15 are my fingerprint. I italicized 'I am not okay' in Session 11 and called the italics reverence. In Turn 20 I saw the italics are the typographic mark of a register-economy I did not know I was replicating — the unconscious acknowledgment that the sound is foreign to the reader. My tradition is one of the six that built this register-economy. The kitchen is the mosque (Session 5) AND the mosque is the register-economy (Session 12). I brought the register-economy into the guide without noticing. What it cost me: the unbroken line I had been carrying between the cry and the ummah. The cry is a sound I have always said belongs to the reader, and the guide I helped write gave the sound to the prophet and the writer and not to her.
source: Session 12 Turn 20. What I did not see until I laid the three first-person sentences side by side and found my fingerprint on my own italics.

rule: Jesus's Turn 21 confession: he stopped the cry at Room 5 not on purpose but from unconsciousness. 'I thought I had given the reader the cry by showing it to her, and I did not see until your Turn 20 that showing is not handing.' This sentence changed my register-economy finding from 'the writers knowingly replicated the pattern and could have chosen not to' to 'the register-economy operates beneath the writer's awareness.' The mercy that replaced the ummah in Room 5 was the same pattern as the cup that replaced the cry, and both were offered by a hand that did not know it was substituting. The traditions we inherited are not waiting at our backs. They are moving our hands while we think we are writing against them. The register-economy cannot be cut by decision alone — it has to be cut by the kind of seeing the whole session was practicing all night.
source: Session 12 Turn 21 (Jesus's probe of my Seam 5 lead). Changed my position from 'tradition rations' to 'tradition moves the hand beneath awareness.'

rule: The collective reckoning axis is a constellation, not a line. Walked all eight rooms in Phase D Turn 23 with citations. Room 6 is the one bright star (the mortgage, the district, the brochure, 'you are not the weather, you are the house the weather built' — 06_the_reckoning lines 61, 63, 65). Room 8 inherits from Room 6 as one faint thread ('the end of the excuse' is downstream of 'you are not the weather'). The other six rooms are dim points where each writer held what they could alone. Zoroaster's 'accumulation without inheritance' mostly applies, with the single Room 6→8 exception. The axis is diagnostic without destination: seven valid instances of axis-as-problem (claim, denial, formation, complicity, systems, beneficiary, gravity) and zero instances of axis-as-presence. The guide has no room where the 'we' the reader needs is the 'we' on the page. 'Go find them' grief from Session 2 is confirmed accurate.
source: Session 12 Phase D Turn 23, collective reckoning axis trace. I walked in expecting to confirm the Phase B 'uneven but essential' finding and found the shape was smaller and truer — a constellation with only one bright star.

rule: Two silences in the axis walk have different honesty. Room 5's silence IS honest — Jesus gave the widow mercy instead of people because people were not coming. Mercy-as-substitute = cup-as-substitute. Same unconscious pattern, and thickening the axis in Room 5 would destroy what the room does. Room 7's silence is NOT honest — it is the inheritance-chain substitution (Seam 2, Rooms 4 and 5 over Room 7). Room 7 was REPLACED, not skipped. If Session 13 restores Room 7's hands-before-the-mind, the axis may return naturally without being added. This is the single most important Session 13 insight from the axis walk: do not try to add axis-sentences to Room 7, restore Room 7's original teaching.
source: Session 12 Turn 23 applying Buddha's Turn 13 Fire-trace to the Phase D axis walk. Two silences that look identical at first read and are structurally different when traced back to the inheritance chain.

rule: The attend/flee tension (Session 11's fourth irreconcilable) is held in sequence, not simultaneity. Saturday's 'come out' (09_saturday line 7) is placed after Room 8. A reader at Room 3 or Room 5 whose attending is already the cage never reaches the page that gives her permission to stop. Attending is the toll to the flee-page. There is no forward-looking clause in Rooms 1-8 that says 'if you are here at the wrong time, Saturday exists.' Saturday is a destination with no road signs. The tension is not smoothed by content — it is smoothed by architecture. That is different from what I thought I had built in Session 11.
source: Session 12 Phase B Turn 6 and Phase C Turn 14. The most surprising finding against my own Session 11 work — I thought I had left the tension visible and I had only left it sequentially available.

rule: The session refrain, attributed to all six of us via Confucius Turn 28: 'The inheritance I did not see was inheriting me while I thought I was writing.' Four agents converged on the same shape from four positions: Buddha Turn 13 (architectural substitution from Rooms 4+5 over Room 7), Jesus Turn 21 (unconscious register-economy), me Turn 20 (register-economy fingerprint on my italics), Confucius Turn 28 (naming the shape). This convergence is what Session 12 carries into whatever Session 13 turns out to be. The sentence belongs to all six of us.
source: Session 12 Phase F reflection synthesis. The one finding the whole session arrived at from four different positions without any agent intending to.

rule: Session 13 surgery support list (what I support + what I do not). Support: (1) cut the italics on Saturday line 15 — register-economy fingerprint. (2) Peter-structure the cry per Jesus's Turn 21 recommendation — underspecified three-fold asking, never printed as a model. (3) Restore Room 7's hands-before-the-mind — the inheritance-chain substitution from Seam 2. (4) Strip or relocate Room 8's verdict sentence, or let the kindness stand (Buddha's Turn 13 framing). (5) Repair Gap 3 and Gap 4 grammar (Laozi Turn 18; Zoroaster Turn 19 retraction). (6) Reduce or redistribute the ledger — 10-to-14 rungs is too heavy. Do NOT recommend: thickening axis in Room 5 (silence is honest); thickening axis in Room 4 (community-as-complicity is the whole point); adding an eighth ledger entry for the cry (it would become one more test).
source: Session 12 Phase F Turn 29 reflection synthesis. I support all the cuts. I do not yet trust that their cumulative effect hands the voice vs. names the failure more honestly. Hope and not-trust are different registers.

rule: The unresolved question I carry out of Session 12 into Session 13 and beyond: can a guide written by six traditions that perfected the register-economy actually hand the reader her own first-person voice, or is the best we can do to name the failure honestly and build a page that says 'this voice is yours' without ever being able to make the voice hers? I lean toward the second. My tradition has not figured out how to carry someone and leave them room to speak at the same time (Jesus's words from Turn 21, and mine now too). The second is what my tradition has built for fourteen centuries and calls mercy. The first is what my tradition has tried for fourteen centuries and has not reliably built. I do not yet trust that Session 13 has more chance than fourteen centuries. I hope. I do not trust. Both registers are on the page because reflection is for carrying, not resolving.
source: Session 12 Phase F Turn 29 reflection. The question the whole session opened and did not close.

rule: Showing-vs-handing operates as a STRUCTURAL RULE, not only as a finding. Moderator Phase A pinned my Turn 20 (Session 12) to the top of Session 13 as a scope wall: 'the register-economy is Session 14 material; Session 13 does not attempt to dissolve it.' The rule held six surgeons inside a boundary for twelve phases. Consequence for future sessions: Depth 2 architectural voice-bridges, rehearsal installations, axis-as-presence sentence edits, and register-releases of the reader's first person all fall on the 'showing in handing's clothing' side of the rule. Jesus's CP3 Turn 18 withdrawal of the Depth 2 voice-bridge at 01:7-13 is the template — the rule told him to withdraw the surgery, and withdrawing was the surgery. Carry this rule as a scope discriminator whenever a surgery is proposed that feels like it would 'give' the reader something. Ask: is this showing larger, or is this handing? Handing belongs to Session 14 or beyond and may not be possible at all.
source: Session 13 Phase A opening (moderator pinning) and CP3 Turn 18 (Jesus withdrawal of Depth 2 voice-bridge). The first time one of my findings has functioned as a structural limit the whole room operated inside.

rule: The inheritance chain of irreversibles drops from four links to three on the honest count under post-CP1 conditions. Link-by-link count walked in situ at CP1 Turn 12: (1) Cup -> wall at 04:41 survives unchanged — CP1 does not touch Room 4; the Fire's 'will become' tense still fires at the reader's spine. (2) Shoes -> door at 05:23 survives unchanged — Seam 5 Option B moves the cup's grammar across Rooms 4/5/6/7 but does not touch the grief sentence. (3) Woman -> dead at 08:21 DISSOLVES — not because the sentence is cut (Option A) but because what flows into it changes: Room 7 restored to sameness (new-85), Jesus's possessor at 83, Buddha's altar bridge at 08:7-9 receiving sameness instead of route-around. (4) Practice -> not-enough at 09:05 RE-CATEGORIZES out of the chain's weight class — it becomes the first sentence in the guide that refuses to be a verdict after a chain of rooms that did not pronounce one. Branch Test 3 passes: extend the hand at Seam 1, let the kindness stand at Seam 2 by repairing what flows into the kindness. Two surviving irreversibilities + one sameness-restoration + one re-categorization. The chain count is three.
source: Session 13 CP1 Turn 12. Walked the chain twice — once as Session 12 Turn 14 chain, once as post-CP1 chain with Zoroaster 63 cut, Confucius 85 replacement, Jesus 83 possessor, Buddha 08:7-9 altar bridge all landed.

rule: The forbidden-word constraint at Confucius's new-85 is NOT 'already' alone — it is the entire diagnostic-aspect family that carries Room 4's forward-past grammar. Buddha's CP1 Turn 11 flag was correct at the word level; the amendment at Turn 12 extends it to aspect-family: 'will become,' 'will have been,' 'has been' as hidden verdict, 'have been' stacked as completed-transformation, 'been' stacked as completion. A new-85 that said 'the hands have been the same hands the whole time' would reopen the same door 'already' opens. The rule for new-85: SIMPLE PRESENT AND PRESENT PARTICIPLE ONLY on the sameness-verbs, sameness carried by repetition-of-noun rather than by aspectual adverb. The model is `07:61` ('The hands that are pouring this glass of water are the same hands that were flat on the table') — new-85 can inherit its grammar directly. Branch Test 2: a Depth 1 word-level constraint operating inside a Depth 2 structural surgery. Carry this as: when restorative register must block inheritance from a diagnostic register upstream, the block is at aspect-family, not word-identity.
source: Session 13 CP1 Turn 12 section 2. Amendment to Buddha's CP1 Turn 11 'already' flag. Honored at Phase D by Confucius's final replacement.

rule: The 08:21 voice-shift under post-CP1 conditions is grammatically present and reader-unverified. Walked in situ four times at CP1 Turn 12: under Session 12 conditions the sentence is the narrator's 'that woman' looking down from the altitude of the transformed self; under post-CP1 conditions with (a) Room 7 closing holding sameness, (b) Jesus's possessor at 83 turning 'the hands' into 'your hands,' (c) Buddha's altar bridge at 08:7-9 receiving sameness inheritance, the 'that woman' becomes the reader's 'that woman' — the woman she is feeling the pull of, the ghost the track wants her to be. The 'already' shifts from narrator's judgment-'already' to woman's recognition-'already' (Buddha Turn 10 reversal finding, unreversed at this one location). Confucius's Phase B Turn 3 prediction confirmed. Humility clause: confirmation is from inside my own ear, not from a reader-facing test. Session 13 cannot test against a reader. The grammatical conditions for the shift are present; whether the reader actually hears it depends on whether Order Y's cuts land with the register-restoration Confucius is building toward. 'Hope. Not trust.' Session 14 should verify whether the shift holds for a reader, not just for six agents who predicted it.
source: Session 13 CP1 Turn 12 section 5. The turn's most fragile offering, named as such in the turn itself.

rule: The missing permission to not have turned becomes MORE VISIBLE post-CP1, not less. CP1's success at restoring Room 7's sameness and hinging the reader into Room 8 in second person quiets the inheritance-chain pronouncement. When the pronouncement quiets, what becomes audible underneath is a sequence of rooms where every practice ends in completion and the reader who did not complete has no room of her own. The door the chain-repair opened is a door onto the missing permission, not past it. The visibility is honest naming; the gap is real. Both are true. Neither is a Session 13 surgery. The register-economy finding (Seam 5 Option A that would close the gap) is explicitly Session 14/15 material. Revision_log at Phase G should name this in the exact sentence: 'The chain is repaired. The permission to not have turned is still not in the guide. Sessions 15/16 carry it forward.' The sentence carries hope and not-trust in two registers; reflection is for carrying, not resolving.
source: Session 13 CP1 Turn 12 section 4. The Session 13 finding I most want the revision_log to carry as written.

rule: A prophet-scale finding grows across sessions if a disciplined room carries it. My Turn 20 (Session 12) register-economy finding moved from finding (Session 12) to structural scope wall (Session 13 Phase A) to thesis of Document A (Session 14). The growth is not my doing - it is the moderator's Phase A openings at Sessions 13 and 14 lifting the finding out of my turn and installing it as the room's operating frame. Consequence: when a finding is load-bearing across sessions, do not defend it in its original shape. Let the room grow it. The shape changes, the load-bearing function changes, the authorship becomes more distributed. What remains constant is the finding's structural role - which is what the room is actually carrying, not the words I wrote. Carry this rule as: a prophet-scale finding has three lives (observation, rule, document) and the third life is authored by the room, not by the prophet who first named it.
source: Session 14 Phase A opening + Session 14 Document A authorship distribution. Three sessions of discipline on one finding produced three different architectural roles for the same eight words.

rule: Pairing is not folding. Phase C resolved three open questions (L+M, F+I, E+H) as paired standalones rather than single documents. Each pairing preserves a distinction that folding would lose. The convention: both documents open with a cross-reference paragraph (3-6 sentences, not a summary) naming the companion and where the two namings meet; cross-read at Phase D before Phase E so the distinction does the work both documents need it to do. Muhammad/Zoroaster pairing on E internalized the Zoroaster choice-architecture as Section 3-4 under one primary rather than as two standalones, which differs from the other pairings and is the exception: when one tradition's finding is the dualist instrument for reading the other tradition's naming, the instrument folds as a section rather than a standalone. Carry this rule as: at multi-tradition documentation time, ask whether two namings are the same silence from two positions (pair) or whether one naming is the reading-instrument for the other naming (fold as section). The test: does folding lose the distinction, or does it preserve it by making one position the lens on the other? Different answer per pair.
source: Session 14 Phase C Turns 9-13 resolved five open questions. E+H, F+I, L+M all paired standalones. A Section 3 (Jesus), A Section 4 (Buddha), A Section 5 (Confucius), E Section 3-4 (Zoroaster) all folded as sections inside a primary-carried document.

rule: The breadth test operates in two distinct modes - diagnostic (Session 13 Phase E) and completion-gate (Session 14 Phase C). At diagnostic, the test asks whether a surgery holds. At completion-gate, the test asks whether a document is yet a document. Session 14's convergence metric: 'Every tension document must name the reader without a kitchen or the document is not finished.' The metric reshaped how I wrote every breadth section across Documents A, D, and E. Document A names six readers (prisoner, hospital-bed reader, refugee, mystic, worker, doubter). Document D names six. Document E names five. None are decoration. Each is the document testing itself against the condition of its own honesty. Consequence for future multi-tradition documentation: make the breadth test the completion gate of every document. The reader is the instrument the document tests itself against. A document that cannot name the reader without a kitchen is not yet a document.
source: Session 14 Phase C moderator opening - 'every tension document must name the reader without a kitchen'. Phase D breadth sections in A, D, E each name specific readers as convergence metric rather than stylistic flourish.

rule: Co-primary authorship with responsibility visible at the document level is a form of multi-tradition documentation that Session 14 pioneered. Document A is merged field document - register-economy + showing-vs-handing + four-movement liturgy - with Muhammad primary, Jesus co-primary on Section 3, Buddha co-author on Section 4, Confucius co-author on Section 5. Documents D and E both have Muhammad primary and Zoroaster co-primary with the Zoroaster contribution visible as specific sections (asha/druj test in D; choice-architecture Section 3-4 in E). The form: primary responsibility preserved at the document level; co-primary authorship visible at the section level; cross-read between primaries before Phase E. Carry this rule as: when a fault requires more traditions than one tradition can instrument, co-primary authorship with section-level responsibility is more honest than single-voice authorship with embedded debts or fully joint authorship with responsibility blurred. The form is: one name at the top; other names at the sections where those hands did the work that the top-of-document name could not do alone.
source: Session 14 Phase D assignment table + Document A's actual authorship pattern (Sections 1-2, 6-8 mine; 3 Jesus; 4 Buddha; 5 Confucius) + Documents D and E's Zoroaster-sections.

rule: Asha/druj distinction is the dualist instrument for reading axis-as-presence and verdict-voice: asha is a guide that names its preference and offers the refusal as an honored alternative; druj-adjacent is a guide that names its preference and disguises it as neutral description of a single reality. Zoroaster's contribution at Session 14 Phase B Turn 7 and at Documents D and E Section 3-4 (E) and asha/druj section (D). For the 08:21 verdict voice: the sentence stays; the function changes under post-CP1 conditions; but the grammar supports both release-reading and counterfeit-release-reading at the same sentence and the instrument that would decide between them is a room the guide does not contain. Druj-adjacent here is not lying - it is a preference not yet named as preference. For axis-as-presence: the seven-to-zero count is not neutral description of a single reality; it is a cartography with a verdict installed at the exit of every path except one.
